case_study_packaging.headline: Outpatient addiction treatment network captures $412K in annual savings and 1.6× ROI through Treya-led sourcing overhaul
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: SaVida Health’s rapid, PE-backed expansion to 20+ clinics left it with a decentralized, low-maturity purchasing model. Vendor contracts, pricing and data were fragmented across locations, obscuring more than $5 million in annual indirect and clinical support spend. With Council Capital targeting margin improvement and near-term value creation, SaVida needed a partner to quickly uncover savings while safeguarding clinical operations and growth plans.
case_study_packaging.client_problem_anonymized: A rapidly expanding outpatient addiction treatment network with 20+ clinics operated with a decentralized, low-maturity purchasing model. Vendor contracts, pricing and data were fragmented across locations, obscuring more than $5 million in annual indirect and clinical support spend. With the private equity ownership group focusing on operational efficiency and margin improvement, the organization needed a partner to quickly uncover savings while safeguarding clinical operations and growth plans.
approach_summary: Analyzed $5.3 M in spend across 10 indirect and clinical support categories to confirm $4.3 M in addressable opportunity.
Renegotiated the client’s Athenahealth EMR contract via a competitive RFP and benchmarking process, cutting fees from 4.56 % to 3.40 %.
Enrolled the client in Provista’s group purchasing organization, securing double-digit price reductions on high-usage medical and office supply SKUs.
Developed an IT hardware sourcing strategy using competitive VAR quotes and GPO leverage to standardize specs and lower unit costs.
Launched a telecom consolidation program to migrate 40+ site-level Comcast accounts into a single managed-services agreement, optimizing bandwidth and pricing.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $412,065 in validated annual run-rate savings—squarely within the upper end of the original $240–$470 K target range—and locked in $357,889 of that total within the first seven months. The savings generate a 1.6× return on Treya’s hybrid fees, surpassing the 1.2× guarantee, while new GPO enrollment, standardized IT specs and a consolidated telecom platform establish sustainable procurement processes for future growth.
where_we_were_unique: Healthcare IT negotiation expertise drove a 22 % reduction on the mission-critical Athenahealth EMR platform.
Preferred access to Provista GPO unlocked pricing tiers the client could not achieve independently.
Hands-on data collection overcame fragmented AP records and supplier non-responsiveness to build an actionable baseline.
Hybrid fee structure aligned incentives and guaranteed savings, ultimately delivering 33 % more ROI than the contractual minimum.
